statement: You are given a directed graph, made of a vertex count n (vertices numbered 0 to n − 1) and a list of edges [u, v], each an edge from u to v.

Decide whether the graph contains a directed cycle. Use Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly remove a vertex with no incoming edges and delete its outgoing edges. A vertex on a cycle never runs out of incoming edges, so if fewer than n vertices are removed, a cycle exists.
Return true if the graph has a directed cycle and false otherwise.

examples.explanation: Vertices 0 and 1 can be removed, but 2 and 3 point at each other, so neither ever loses its last incoming edge. Only 2 of 4 vertices are removed.
All 4 vertices are removed in turn (0, then 1 and 2, then 3), so the graph has no cycle.
The chain 0 → 1 → 2 is removed completely, but the pair 3 ⇄ 4 forms a cycle in a separate part of the graph.
